newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ building consents rise 7.5 pct in year to July.
newsitem.headline: NZ building consents rise 7.5 pct in year to July.

text.p: The total value of New Zealand building consents for the year ended July 1996 was NZ$5.880 billion, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
This was a an increase of 7.5 percent from the $5.468 billion issued in the year ended July 1995.
"Consents for non-residential buildings show no sign of falling from the high level maintained since late 1994," SNZ said in a statement.
Consents with a total value of $2.302 billion were authorised for non-residential buildings in the year ended July 1996, an increase of 10.0 percent from the year ended July 1995.
The value of non-residential consents for the month of July 1996 was $173 million.
The total value of consents for residential buildings in July 1996 was $289.9 million.
Consents for 1,836 new dwelling units were issued in July 1996.
SNZ said the national median consent value for new dwelling units authorised in July 1996 was $120,000, an increase of 3.0 percent when compared with the July 1995 figure.
